title: Dissipative one-carrier barriers and finite diagnostics
analyticalQuestion: How do the rigorous moment, action, scalar-screen, and true-cubic results compare with the two finite dissipative routes?
supportedTakeaway: The rigorous moment barrier and first-layer action lower bound make the action-poor scalar route fail, whereas the project corollary derived from Coble–He Theorem 1.2 gives a sublinear square-root true-cubic bound. Finite normalized proxies suggest but do not prove a logarithmic refinement.
analyticClaims: The complete dissipative one-carrier chain satisfies sup D <= max(1,(2 sigma)^(2/3)).
The critical-log action is at least of order sigma^(-2/3) log sigma, while the actual enstrophy contrast is at most of order 1+sigma^(2/3).
The inherited action-poor ratio sigma^(1/3) x/K is at least of order sigma log sigma and diverges.
The exact scalar term satisfies T_sigma asymptotic in order to V_sigma, both of order sigma^(1/3), with the exact ceiling T/V <= 1.
The project-specific corollary derived from Coble–He Theorem 1.2 gives C_diss <= C a^2 sigma^(1/2), hence C_diss=o(sigma a^2).
finiteDiagnostics: Producer angular-FFT exact-mixing and independent finite-real-chain fourth-order Taylor exponential routes evaluate the same ten sigma cases in IEEE binary64.
The finite action and scalar-screen curves use mu=a=1, x_proxy=sigma^2 A_sigma, K_proxy=1+D_max, U_proxy=sigma^(7/3), and V_proxy=sigma^(1/3), with fixed geometric constants suppressed.
The finite moment, normalized-proxy, and cubic curves corroborate the proved ledger but are not interval proofs or actual physical ratios.
The near-flat finite values of C_diss/log sigma do not prove logarithmic growth or an asymptotic coefficient.

panelClaims.A: The dark curve is the exact rigorous upper barrier; colored markers are finite route values.
panelClaims.B: Both colored families are finite normalized proxies in the declared mu=a=1 proxy ledger. The theorem states the actual lower-growth orders but supplies no plotted numerical constant.
panelClaims.C: The dark line is the exact algebraic ceiling. Colored markers are finite T_proxy/V_proxy values, not the actual physical ratio.
panelClaims.D: All colored curves are finite values. Only uniform boundedness of the square-root normalization follows from the project corollary derived from Coble–He Theorem 1.2.

renderPolicy.producer: blue solid line with filled circle markers
renderPolicy.independent: ochre dashed line with open square markers

claimBoundary: The analytic statements apply only to the declared fixed-band, row-aligned dissipative one-carrier chain. The plotted producer and independent curves are finite binary64 corroboration, not interval certificates. They do not prove a logarithmic true-cubic law, a multi-carrier or multiscale theorem, a continuation criterion, finite-time singularity, or general three-dimensional Navier-Stokes regularity.
